title: Lesson 9: Unit 3 Assessment, Part II: Using Observations of the Sun to Write Narratives
objective: Students will write the second verse of a narrative poem about the sun using evidence from observations and provide kind, helpful, and specific feedback to peers.

what_is_taught.skill: write a narrative poem based on a model and using evidence
use a verse planner to organize ideas for writing
write complete sentences with correct punctuation
discuss and plan writing collaboratively with a partner
give kind, helpful, and specific feedback to a peer
use sentence frames to support writing when needed
reflect on giving and receiving feedback using a protocol
use anchor charts and notebooks as writing resources
participate in choral singing with movements

what_is_NOT_taught: Independent writing beyond the poem verse
Vocabulary instruction beyond use of anchor charts

student_actions.recognition_identification: identify and recall information from anchor charts and notebooks to support writing
student_actions.oral_production: sing chorally with movements; discuss planning and feedback with partners; share reflections orally
student_actions.written_production: write the second verse of a poem using a verse planner and complete sentences
student_actions.procedural_application: apply writing conventions such as punctuation and sentence structure
student_actions.reasoning_explanation: explain how research and resources support their writing; justify feedback to peers

evidence.quote: Invite students to join you in singing the 'Sun, Moon, and Stars' song and completing the accompanying movements.
Remind them that yesterday they began writing the first verse of their 'What the Sun Sees' poem. Today they will work with the same partner to plan the second verse.
Review each prompt question by reading them aloud.
Remind students that they will first work with a partner to discuss each of these questions.
Prompt students to use their resources as support: -Time of Day anchor chart -Adjectives anchor chart -What the Sun Sees anchor chart -Pages in their Sky notebook that describe the sun at midday
Distribute Sky notebooks and 'What the Sun Sees' verse planners.
Move students into pre-determined pairs and invite pairs to find a quiet location to plan together.
Circulate and support students to reference their notebooks and the various anchor charts.
Using a total participation technique, invite responses from the group:
Tell students that now they will have a chance to independently capture their thinking for verse 2 on the 'What the Sun Sees' verse planner.
Invite students to begin writing and circulate to support them as necessary.

Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner: 'How did you use your research about the sun to help you write your poem?' (My verse planner and my Sky notebook helped me find adjectives to describe the sun.)
Invite students to turn and talk with an elbow partner:
Remind students to use their 'What the Sun Sees' verse planner to help them write verse 2 using complete sentences and correct punctuation.
Offer students specific, positive feedback on their focus when writing verse 2 of their poems.
Tell the writers that today they will share verse 2 of their poem with a partner.
Remind students that when a partner shares his or her work, they are going to give kind, helpful and specific feedback.
Tell students that they are going to use the Pinky Partners protocol to provide feedback to a partner on verse 2.
Guide students through the protocol, encouraging them to use the following frames:
Circulate as students share; prompt them to use the criteria on the High-Quality Work anchor chart when providing feedback.
Offer students specific, positive feedback on their conversations giving feedback to one another.
Invite students to Think-Pair-Share with an elbow partner: 'How did you do giving and receiving feedback?'

teacher_actions.direct_instruction: Model reviewing prompt questions and using anchor charts and notebooks to support writing; model giving specific, positive feedback; model using the Pinky Partners protocol for peer feedback; model cleanup routines.
prompts_that_cue_student_response: How did you use your research about the sun to help you write your poem?
What did you need to remember when writing the first verse of your 'What the Sun Sees' poem?
How did you do giving and receiving feedback?

scope.breadth: writing a narrative poem about the sun using evidence; peer feedback; reflection on feedback process
scope.depth: planning, writing, revising, and reflecting on narrative poem writing and peer feedback

context.stimulus_provided: text and anchor charts about the sun and times of day; verse planner; poem model

sections_covered.warm_up: Engaging the Learner: 'Sun, 'Moon, and Stars' Song
sections_covered.direct_instruction: Review prompt questions and model use of resources; model feedback protocol
sections_covered.guided_practice: Partner planning and discussion; peer feedback using Pinky Partners protocol
sections_covered.independent_application: Writing second verse of poem independently
sections_covered.check_for_understanding: Think-Pair-Share reflection on giving and receiving feedback
sections_covered.differentiated_reinforce: Provide partially filled verse planners and sentence frames for students needing support
sections_covered.differentiated_extend: Encourage paraphrasing learning targets and independent writing before support for ELLs

supports.english_language_learners: Provide sentence frames for writing; encourage paraphrasing learning targets; review use of anchor charts and notebooks; provide guided verse planners; give positive feedback to ELLs
supports.universal_design_udl: Provide options for physical movement during song; use sound-canceling headphones or dividers to minimize distractions; display checklists for peer feedback; use total participation techniques
supports.below_level_reinforce: Provide partially filled-in or guided verse planners; use sentence frames for writing support
supports.above_level_extend: Encourage paraphrasing learning targets; allow grappling with writing before providing sentence frames

assessment.method: Observation of independent writing and peer feedback; Think-Pair-Share reflection

notes: Lesson focuses on writing the second verse of a narrative poem about the sun using evidence from observations and peer feedback. Includes supports for ELLs and students needing additional writing help. Uses multiple anchor charts and notebooks as resources. Incorporates movement and oral language practice through song and partner discussions.
